Definition: from ὄκνος (hesitation); to be slow (figuratively, loath):--delay.
BiblicalUsage: Okneo means to delay, to be slow, to hold back. It occurs once, in Acts 9:38, where the disciples send to Peter desiring him not to delay coming to Lydda.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe delay can cost a life, and the disciples were right to ask Peter to come without holding back.
